subject: math
title: Expressions and Binomials: Like Terms with Integers, Adding Binomials and Evaluating
seo_title: Grade 8 Expressions and Binomials Worksheets: Like Terms and Evaluating (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Add and subtract monomials with a degree of 1, and add binomials with a degree of 1 that involve integers, using tools
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 math worksheets on expressions and binomials for the Ontario curriculum: combining like terms with integers and algebra tiles, adding binomials, subtracting monomials, evaluating expressions with integers and fractions, and perimeter problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Combine only like terms, using integer rules: −3x + 5x = 2x, and (2x + 3) + (x − 5) = 3x − 2.
key_sub: 3x + 2 is not 5x. To subtract, add the opposite: 6x − (−4x) = 10x. To evaluate, put the value in brackets: −3(−2) + 4 = 10.
body_html:
Like terms and zero pairs

Like terms have the same variable part, such as −3x and 5x, or two constants. To combine like terms, add the coefficients and keep the variable. Use integer rules for the signs.

ExpressionAdd the coefficientsResult
−3x + 5x−3 + 5 = 22x
−4x − 6x−4 − 6 = −10−10x
−x + 6x−1 + 6 = 55x

x means 1x, and −x means −1x. Terms that are not alike stay apart: 3x + 2 cannot be simplified.

Add binomials

A binomial has two terms, like 2x + 3. To add binomials, group the x-terms and the constants. Each sign belongs to the term right after it.

Example 1

Add (−6k − 2) + (k + 5).

k-terms: −6 + 1 = −5. Constants: −2 + 5 = 3.

Answer: −5k + 3

Subtract monomials

To subtract, add the opposite: 6x − (−4x) = 6x + 4x = 10x.

Evaluate expressions

Replace the variable with its value in brackets, then follow the order of operations.

Example 2

Evaluate −3x + 4 when x = −2.

−3 × (−2) = 6. Then 6 + 4 = 10.

Answer: 10

Example 3

Evaluate 2x − 34 when x = 58.

2 × 58 = 108. 108 − 68 = 48.

Answer: 12

Perimeter

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
3x + 2 = 5x3x and 2 are not like terms. 3x + 2 is already simplified
−3x + 5x = −8xUse integer rules: −3 + 5 = 2, so 2x
(2x + 3) + (x − 5) = 3x + 8The minus sign belongs to 5: 3 + (−5) = −2
6x − (−4x) = 2xAdd the opposite: 6x + 4x = 10x
(−3)2 = −9(−3) × (−3) = 9
Adding only two sides for a perimeterAdd every side of the shape

faq.q: What do Grade 8 students learn about algebraic expressions in the Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: In Grade 8 (Algebra, C2.1 and C2.2), students add and subtract monomials such as −3x + 5x, add binomials such as (2x + 3) + (x − 5), often with algebra tiles, and evaluate expressions that involve integers, fractions and decimals.

faq.q: How do you add two binomials?
faq.a: Group the like terms and add each group. For (2x + 3) + (x − 5), the x-terms give 3x and the constants give 3 + (−5) = −2, so the sum is 3x − 2.

faq.q: What is a zero pair in algebra tiles?
faq.a: A zero pair is one positive tile and one negative tile of the same kind, such as x and −x. Together they equal 0, so they can be removed or added without changing the value.
It is 2x. Add the coefficients with integer rules: −3 + 5 = 2. −8x is a common sign error.

items.q: What is the coefficient of x in 7 − x?
items.e: −x means −1x, so the coefficient is −1. The minus sign belongs to the term after it. (It is not 0: x on its own is 1x.)

items.q: Green tiles are positive and red tiles are negative. Remove the zero pairs. Which expression do the tiles show?
items.e: Each x-tile and −x-tile make a zero pair. 4 green and 2 red tiles: 2 zero pairs, and 2 green tiles are left: 2x. (6x counts the red tiles as positive.)

items.q: Green tiles are positive and red tiles are negative. Remove the zero pairs. Which expression do the tiles show?
items.e: 1 green tile and 1 red tile make a zero pair. 3 red tiles are left, so the tiles show −3x. (3x forgets that the leftover tiles are negative.)

items.q: Green tiles are positive and red tiles are negative. Remove the zero pairs. Which expression do the tiles show?
items.e: 3 green and 3 red x-tiles make 3 zero pairs, so no x-tiles are left. Only the two 1-tiles are left: 2. (2x joins the 2 to the x-tiles.)

items.q: Green tiles are positive and red tiles are negative. Remove the zero pairs. Which expression do the tiles show?
items.e: x-tiles: 5 green and 2 red leave 3x. 1-tiles: 1 yellow and 3 red leave −2. The tiles show 3x − 2. (x joins 3x and −2, which are not like terms.)

items.q: Green tiles are positive and red tiles are negative. Remove the zero pairs. Which expression do the tiles show?
items.e: x-tiles: 2 green and 5 red leave −3x. 1-tiles: 4 yellow and 1 red leave 3. The tiles show −3x + 3. (7x + 5 counts every tile as positive.)
Add the coefficients: −3 + 5 = 2, so −3x + 5x = 2x. (−8x and 8x add 3 and 5 and ignore the signs.)
−4 − 6 = −10, so the answer is −10x. (−2x subtracts 4 from 6 instead.)
7 − 9 = −2, so 7x − 9x = −2x. The result is negative because 9 is greater than 7.
−x means −1x: −1 + 6 = 5, so the answer is 5x. (6x treats −x as 0. 7x drops the minus sign.)
−8 + 3 = −5, so −8n + 3n = −5n. The variable stays. (−5 drops the n.)
Left to right: 2 − 7 = −5, then −5 + 4 = −1. So the answer is −1y = −y. (−9y subtracts the 4y too.)
−k means −1k: −5 − 1 = −6, so the answer is −6k. (−4k adds the 1 instead of subtracting it.)
9 − 12 = −3, then −3 − 1 = −4. So the answer is −4m. (−3m forgets the last −m.)
x-terms: 3 − 5 = −2, so −2x. Constants: −4 + 9 = 5. The answer is −2x + 5. (8x + 5 ignores the minus sign in front of 5x.)
a-terms: −6 + 4 = −2, so −2a. Constants: 2 − 7 = −5. The answer is −2a − 5. (−7a joins unlike terms.)
y-terms: −2 + 8 = 6, so 6y. Constants: 5 − 11 = −6. The answer is 6y − 6. (0 joins 6y and −6, which are not like terms.)
x-terms: 1 − 3 = −2, so −2x. Constants: −8 − 1 = −9. The answer is −2x − 9. (−3x − 9 forgets that x is 1x.)
7m − 7m = 0m = 0, so the m-terms cancel. Constants: −4 − 2 = −6. The answer is −6. (−6m keeps a variable that is no longer there.)

items.q: Leah says −3x + 2 = −x. Test it with x = 4. What are the values of −3x + 2 and −x?
items.e: −3x + 2 = −3 × 4 + 2 = −12 + 2 = −10, but −x = −4. The values are different, so Leah is wrong: −3x and 2 are not like terms.

items.q: The algebra tiles show (2x + 3) + (x + 1). Green tiles are positive and red tiles are negative. What is the sum?
items.e: x-tiles: 2 + 1 = 3, so 3x. 1-tiles: 3 + 1 = 4. The sum is 3x + 4. (2x + 4 forgets the single x-tile.)

items.q: The algebra tiles show (2x + 3) + (x − 5). Green tiles are positive and red tiles are negative. What is the sum?
items.e: x-tiles: 2 + 1 = 3, so 3x. 1-tiles: 3 yellow and 5 red make 3 zero pairs, and 2 red are left: −2. The sum is 3x − 2. (3x + 8 counts the red tiles as positive.)

items.q: The algebra tiles show (3x − 4) + (−x + 2). Green tiles are positive and red tiles are negative. What is the sum?
items.e: x-tiles: 3 green and 1 red leave 2x. 1-tiles: 4 red and 2 yellow leave −2. The sum is 2x − 2. (4x − 2 counts the red x-tile as positive.)

items.q: The algebra tiles show (−2x + 1) + (4x + 3). Green tiles are positive and red tiles are negative. What is the sum?
items.e: x-tiles: 2 red and 4 green leave 2x. 1-tiles: 1 + 3 = 4. The sum is 2x + 4. (6x + 4 counts the red x-tiles as positive. 6x joins unlike terms.)
x-terms: 4x + 2x = 6x. Constants: 7 − 3 = 4. The sum is 6x + 4. (6x + 10 ignores the minus sign in 2x − 3.)
n-terms: 5n + 3n = 8n. Constants: −2 + (−6) = −8. The sum is 8n − 8. (8n − 4 subtracts 2 from 6 instead of adding two negatives.)
y-terms: −3 + 5 = 2, so 2y. Constants: 8 − 1 = 7. The sum is 2y + 7. (8y + 7 drops the minus sign of −3y.)
x + x = 2x, not x2. Constants: −9 + 4 = −5. The sum is 2x − 5.
k-terms: −6 + 1 = −5, so −5k. Constants: −2 + 5 = 3. The sum is −5k + 3. (−6k + 3 forgets that k is 1k.)
a-terms: 7 + (−7) = 0, so they cancel. Constants: 4 + 6 = 10. The sum is 10. (10a keeps a variable that has cancelled.)
m-terms: 2 + (−8) = −6, so −6m. Constants: −5 + (−3) = −8. The sum is −6m − 8. (10m − 8 drops the minus sign of −8m.)
t-terms: −4 + (−2) = −6, so −6t. Constants: 9 + (−9) = 0. The sum is −6t.
x-terms: 3 + 1 + 2 = 6, so 6x. Constants: 2 − 4 + 5 = 3. The sum is 6x + 3. (5x + 3 forgets that x is 1x.)
Match like terms even when the order is different. x-terms: −2 + (−3) = −5. Constants: 6 + 5 = 11. The sum is −5x + 11.
y-terms: 4y + 2y = 6y. Constants: 6 − 10 = −4. The sum is 6y − 4. (2y joins unlike terms.)
x-terms: −1 + (−1) = −2. Constants: −1 + (−1) = −2. The sum is −2x − 2. (0 treats two equal terms as a zero pair, but a zero pair needs opposite terms.)

items.q: Which binomial must be added to 2x + 3 to get 5x − 1?
items.e: x-terms: 2 + ? = 5, so 3x. Constants: 3 + ? = −1, so −4. Check: (2x + 3) + (3x − 4) = 5x − 1. (7x + 2 adds instead.)

items.q: Which binomial must be added to −4x + 6 to get x + 2?
Which binomial must be added to x − 7 to get 4x + 1?
Noah added (5x − 3) + (−2x + 4) and got 7x + 1. What mistake did he make?
c: He ignored the minus sign of −2x.
items.e: 5x + (−2x) = 3x, not 7x. The constants are right: −3 + 4 = 1. The correct sum is 3x + 1.
8 − 3 = 5, so 8x − 3x = 5x. The variable stays.
3 − 8 = −5, so 3x − 8x = −5x. (5x subtracts the wrong way round.)
−2 − 5 = −7, so the answer is −7x. Going down from −2 by 5 gives −7. (−3x subtracts 2 from 5.)
x means 1x: 1 − 4 = −3, so the answer is −3x. (−4x treats x as 0.)
y means 1y: −6 − 1 = −7, so the answer is −7y. (−5y adds the 1.)

items.q: To find 2x − (−3x), start with 2 green tiles. There are no red tiles to take away, so add 3 zero pairs, then take away 3 red tiles. What is left?
items.e: After the 3 red tiles are taken away, 2 + 3 = 5 green tiles are left: 2x − (−3x) = 5x. Subtracting a negative is the same as adding its opposite: 2x + 3x. (−x works out 2 − 3.)

items.q: The tiles show −4x − (−x): start with 4 red tiles and take away 1 red tile. What is left?
items.e: 4 red tiles take away 1 red tile leaves 3 red tiles: −4x − (−x) = −3x. (−5x takes away a green tile instead of a red one.)
Subtracting −4x is the same as adding 4x: 6x + 4x = 10x. (2x subtracts 4x instead.)
Add the opposite: −5x + 2x = −3x. (−7x subtracts 2x instead of adding it.)
Add the opposite: −3n + 8n = 5n. (−11n subtracts 8n instead of adding it.)
Add the opposite: 2a + a = 2a + 1a = 3a. (a subtracts instead. 2a treats −a as 0.)
Constants are monomials too. Add the opposite: −9 + 4 = −5. (−13 subtracts 4 instead of adding it.)
Only 5x is a like term with 2x: 5x − 2x = 3x. The 4 stays: 3x + 4. (3x + 2 takes 2 from the constant as well.)
2x − 6x = −4x. The −3 stays: −4x − 3. (−7x joins unlike terms.)
Add the opposite: −x + 5x = 4x. The 7 stays: 4x + 7. (4x + 2 takes 5 from the constant too.)
4y − 9y = −5y. Then −5y − (−2y) = −5y + 2y = −3y. (−7y subtracts 2y instead of adding it.)
−3 − 2 − 1 = −6, so the answer is −6m. (−5m treats −m as 0.)
“Subtract −6k from 2k” means 2k − (−6k) = 2k + 6k = 8k. (−8k works out −6k − 2k, the wrong order.)

items.q: What is the difference when 3x is subtracted from −7x?
items.e: Start with −7x and take away 3x: −7x − 3x = −10x. (−4x adds 3x instead.)

sets.title: Evaluate expressions with integers and fractions

items.e: −3 × (−2) = 6, because a negative times a negative is positive. Then 6 + 4 = 10. (−2 comes from −3 × (−2) = −6, a sign error. −1 adds −3 + (−2) + 4.)
5 × (−3) = −15. Then −15 − 7 = −22. (−8 adds the 7 instead of subtracting it. 8 uses +15.)
−2 × (−6) = 12. Then 12 − 9 = 3. (−21 comes from the sign error −2 × (−6) = −12.)
(−3)2 = (−3) × (−3) = 9. Then 9 + 4 = 13. (−5 uses −9 for the square. −2 reads x2 as 2x.)
Square first: (−2)<sup>2</sup> = 4. Then 2 × 4 = 8, and 8 − 5 = 3. (11 squares 2 × (−2). −13 uses −4 for the square. −9 forgets to square.)
4 − (−6) = 4 + 6 = 10. (−2 works out 4 − 6, losing the minus sign of −6.)
xy = −4 × 3 = −12. Then −12 − 6 = −18. (6 uses +12. −7 adds the values instead of multiplying. 18 drops the minus sign.)
34 × 12: 12 ÷ 4 = 3, then 3 × 3 = 9. (16 divides by 3 and multiplies by 4. 36 forgets to divide by 4.)
Divide first: −15 ÷ 5 = −3. Then −3 + 2 = −1. (5 makes the quotient positive. −3 forgets the + 2.)

items.q: Evaluate x + 12 when x = 13.
items.e: Use a common denominator: 26 + 36 = 56. (25 adds the tops and the bottoms. 16 multiplies.)

items.q: Evaluate 2x − 34 when x = 58.
items.e: 2 × 58 = 108. Then 108 − 68 = 48 = 12. (−18 doubles the bottom as well: 1016. 2 adds 34 instead of subtracting.)
−23 × (−9): 9 ÷ 3 = 3, then 2 × 3 = 6. Negative × negative is positive, so the answer is 6. (−13 12 multiplies by 32 instead of 23.)

items.q: Evaluate 4y + 12 when y = −34.
items.e: 4 × (−34) = −3. Then −3 + 12 = −2 12. (−3 12 subtracts the 12. 516 multiplies only the bottom by 4.)
−1.5 × 4 = −6. Then −6 + 2 = −4. (8 drops the minus sign. 4.5 adds −1.5 + 4 + 2.)
Multiply first: 3 × 1.5 = 4.5. Then 2.5 − 4.5 = −2. ((2.5 − 3) × 1.5 = −0.75 subtracts first. 2 subtracts the wrong way round.)
Simplify first: 3x − 2. Then 3 × (−4) − 2 = −12 − 2 = −14. (−4 uses 3x + 8, ignoring the minus sign of 5. −10 uses 3x + 2. 10 uses +12.)

items.q: Which expression has a value of −7 when x = −2?
Which expression gives the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: Add all four sides: (2x + 3) + (x − 1) + (2x + 3) + (x − 1). x-terms: 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 6. Constants: 3 − 1 + 3 − 1 = 4. The perimeter is 6x + 4. (3x + 2 adds only two sides.)

items.q: Which expression gives the perimeter of the triangle?
items.e: x-terms: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6. Constants: 4 − 1 + 2 = 5. The perimeter is 6x + 5. (6x + 7 ignores the minus sign of 1.)

items.q: Which expression gives the perimeter of the square?
items.e: A square has 4 equal sides: (3x − 2) + (3x − 2) + (3x − 2) + (3x − 2) = 12x − 8. (12x − 2 subtracts the 2 only once. 6x − 4 adds two sides.)

items.q: Which expression gives the perimeter of the triangle?
items.e: x-terms: 2 + 2 + 1 = 5. Constants: 5 + 5 − 3 = 7. The perimeter is 5x + 7. (5x + 13 ignores the minus sign of 3. 3x + 2 adds each different side only once.)

items.q: Which expression gives the perimeter of the regular hexagon?
items.e: A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides. Adding x + 2 six times gives 6x and 6 × 2 = 12: 6x + 12. (6x + 2 adds the 2 only once.)

items.q: Which expression gives the perimeter of the rectangle?
Which expression gives the perimeter of the triangle?
items.e: x-terms: 5 + 3 + 1 = 9. Constants: −2 − 4 + 9 = 3. The perimeter is 9x + 3. (9x − 15 subtracts the 9 as well.)

items.q: A rectangle has length (2x + 3) cm and width (x − 1) cm. What is its perimeter when x = 6?
items.e: The perimeter is 6x + 4. When x = 6: 6 × 6 + 4 = 40, so 40 cm. (20 cm adds only two sides. 75 multiplies 15 × 5, which is the area.)

items.q: Mei is x years old. Ethan is 3 years older than Mei. Which expression gives the sum of their ages?
items.e: Ethan is x + 3. The sum is x + (x + 3) = 2x + 3. (x + 3 is only Ethan’s age.)

items.q: At 6:00 a.m. the temperature in Winnipeg is t °C. By noon it rises 9 °C. By midnight it falls 14 °C from the noon temperature. Which expression gives the midnight temperature?
items.e: t + 9 − 14 = t − 5. A rise is +9 and a fall is −14, and 9 − 14 = −5. (t − 23 treats the rise as a fall.)

items.q: The midnight temperature is (t − 5) °C. What is it when the 6:00 a.m. temperature t is −12 °C?
items.e: −12 − 5 = −17, so −17 °C. Going down 5 degrees from −12 gives a colder temperature. (−7 goes up 5 degrees instead. 11 uses t + 23. 17 drops the minus sign.)

items.q: The Grade 8 class sells mugs at a winter fair. They paid $45 for printing and earn $3 on each mug, so their profit is 3m − 45 dollars for m mugs. What is the profit if they sell 12 mugs?
items.e: 3 × 12 = 36. Then 36 − 45 = −9. A profit of −$9.00 means they lost $9.00. ($81.00 adds the $45 instead of subtracting it.)

items.q: Liam has 4x + 6 hockey cards and Owen has 2x − 1 hockey cards. Which expression gives the number of cards they have altogether?
items.e: (4x + 6) + (2x − 1): x-terms 4 + 2 = 6, constants 6 − 1 = 5. Altogether: 6x + 5. (11x joins unlike terms.)

items.q: Kai paddles x km on Monday, (x + 2) km on Tuesday and (2x − 3) km on Wednesday on a canoe trip. Which expression gives his total distance in kilometres?
items.e: x + (x + 2) + (2x − 3): x-terms 1 + 1 + 2 = 4, constants 2 − 3 = −1. Total: 4x − 1. (3x − 1 forgets Monday’s x.)

items.q: Kai’s total distance is (4x − 1) km. How far does he paddle in all when x = 3?
Sofia is x years old. Her brother is 4 years younger than she is, and her cousin is twice as old as Sofia. Which expression gives the sum of the three ages?
items.e: Sofia x, brother x − 4, cousin 2x. Sum: x + (x − 4) + 2x = 4x − 4. (4x + 4 makes the brother older instead of younger.)

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 10x + 6. Its length is 3x + 2. Which expression gives its width?
items.e: Length + width is half the perimeter: 5x + 3. Width: (5x + 3) − (3x + 2) = 2x + 1. Check: 2(3x + 2) + 2(2x + 1) = 10x + 6. (4x + 2 forgets to halve.)

items.q: A triangle has a perimeter of 9x − 2. Two of its sides are 2x + 3 and 4x − 1. Which expression gives the third side?
items.e: The two sides add to 6x + 2. The third side is 9x − 2 minus that: 3x − 4. Check: (2x + 3) + (4x − 1) + (3x − 4) = 9x − 2. (3x − 2 subtracts only the x-terms.)

items.q: At a hockey game, an adult ticket costs x dollars and a student ticket costs $6 less. Which expression gives the cost of 2 adult tickets and 3 student tickets?
items.e: x + x + (x − 6) + (x − 6) + (x − 6): x-terms 5x, constants −6 three times = −18. Total: 5x − 18. (5x − 6 takes $6 off only once.)

items.q: The tickets cost (5x − 18) dollars. What is the total cost when an adult ticket costs $15?
